newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France Hahn hub to speed cargo at CDG.
newsitem.headline: Air France Hahn hub to speed cargo at CDG.

text.p: Air France said its new German air cargo road trucking hub at Hahn airport would speed up freight transport to and through Charles de Gaulle airport.
Airfreight from six Air France stations in Germany could now be palletised at Hahn for specific destinations worldwide within three hours and then rapidly transhipped through Paris, a statement said.
German consignments were previously sent unsorted to Paris where they then had to be re-palletised for onward transport on long-haul freighter flights.
Otto Meyer, the airline's Germany cargo director, said: "This new logistics makes us faster and more competitive, especially for small and medium-sized consignments".
The hub, which opened at the start of July, has a capacity to handle at least 60,000 tonnes of airfreight a year in a 6,500 sq m freight terminal and has 20 loading doors.
Investor Hahn holding, the owner and manager of the airport, invested eight million marks in the building, which was constructed in five months, the statement said.
Hahn airport is a former U.S. military airport in Rhineland-Palatinate which is seeking to establish itself as an airport for heavy lift cargo and logistics operations.
